newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wharf says no decision on ADS appeal.
newsitem.headline: Wharf says no decision on ADS appeal.

text.p: Wharf (Holdings) Ltd said on Thursday it had not yet decided whether to appeal a Hong Kong court decision in March to award about HK$225 million against it.
Gary Shing, head of corporate affairs at Wharf and parent Wheelock and Co Ltd, told Reuters that the company was still waiting for legal advice on the Wheelock Marden case.

In March, Wharf said a Danish finance institution, ADS, had been awarded about HK$225 million plus interest due to omissions by a former director of Wheelock Marden & Co to supply certain information to ADS.
Wharf took over Wheelock Marden in the mid-1980s. Both unlisted Wheelock Marden and listed Wharf (Holdings) are subsidiaries of Wheelock and Co.

Wharf also said in a statement on Thursday that it intended to fight a US$125.5 million Denver federal district court judgement against it, its Wharf Communications Investments Ltd and managing director Stephen Ng.
Shing declined to comment on the Denver judgement.
Garmen Chan, external affairs director with Wharf Communications Investments Ltd, said he was waiting to hear back from the group's U.S. lawyers about the Denver case.
Chan said he could not expand on a reference in Wharf's statement on the Denver court verdict to "two more claims pending" in the Denver court.
Wharf shares were down HK$0.50 at HK$28.80 at midday Thursday.
